newsitem.title: UK: Sterling jumps to new 4-1/2 year peaks above 2.80 marks.
newsitem.headline: Sterling jumps to new 4-1/2 year peaks above 2.80 marks.

text.p: Sterling scaled new 4-1/2 year peaks on Friday after tearing through key market resistance at 2.80 marks and extending its assault on a generally feeble mark, helped by strength in the dollar.
"People are selling the mark...Sterling/mark is coat-tailing on the back of the mark selling," said Chris Tinker, chief treasury economist at Standard Chartered.

Sterling's strong performance this week, after a rally of nearly two percent against the mark, was crowned on Friday as it jumped to a fresh peak of 2.8034 marks - its highest level since September 1992, when it was ejected from Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).
The pound first moved back above its old ERM floor of 2.7780 marks on Monday.
By 1300 GMT it had slipped back to around 2.8005 marks from an earlier peak of 2.8037 but was still above its level of 2.7891 marks in late European business on Thursday.
Against the strong dollar, sterling was little changed, trading at $1.6245 versus $1.6227 late on Thursday.

Tinker said if the pound's gains against the mark had been related to specific factors affecting the British currency rather than weakness of the mark, it would have been much firmer against the dollar.
"The fact that it hasn't suggests that we are just seeing a mark correction," said Tinker.

Revived optimism that European economic and monetary Union (EMU) will get off the ground as scheduled in 1999 has prompted some mark jitters, driving the German currency to fresh 45-month lows against the French franc overnight and new lows against the peseta and escudo, analysts said.
European Union Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy on Friday said he expected economic and monetary union to start on schedule with many countries.
"It is clear that EMU will become reality starting January 1, 1999 and that a significant number of countries will join then," he told a news conference while on a visit to Finland.
"There is no turning back," he said.

Traders said the Bank of England's offers for a fixed rate round of operations, unchanged at 6.0 percent, implied that Chancellor Kenneth Clarke had decided to leave interest rates unchanged after Thursday's monthly monetary meeting.
But the pound's attractiveness as a high-yielding currency, with its current 10-year yield spread over Germany at 1.85 percentage point the highest in Europe, is clear.

Also in line with forecasts was a poll on Friday showing that the ruling Conservative Party had made only a modest dent in the opposition Labour Party's opinion-poll lead ahead of the British election on May 1.
A Harris poll commissioned for The Independent newspaper on Friday gave Labour a 22-point lead, compared with 24 points the previous week.
